sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know reported statements from B1 Unit 13: after a past verb such as *dijo que*, the verb inside the report moves one step back. The *presente* becomes the *imperfecto*, the *indefinido* and the *perfecto* become the *pluscuamperfecto*, and the *futuro* becomes the *condicional*. You also met the time words that move with them (*mañana* → *al día siguiente*) in B1 Unit 33 and B1 Unit 38. This lesson keeps that pattern and adds a B2 question: when does the verb not have to move?

sections.title: The shift in one place
rows: Dijo que trabajaba en una oficina.
Dijo que había llegado el día anterior.
Dijo que había terminado el informe.
Dijo que llegaría al día siguiente.

sections.title: Two tenses that stay
sections.content: The *imperfecto* and the *pluscuamperfecto* have nowhere further back to go, so they stay as they are (the last two rows).

sections.title: New: when the verb can stay
sections.content:
Moving the verb back is the safe default, and the only choice when you tell a story about the past. But Spanish lets you keep the original tense when what was said is still true, or still to come, at the moment you report it:

• **Still true:** *Me dijo que vive en Lima.* Keeping *vive* says that it is true now. *Me dijo que vivía en Lima* is also correct, but it does not say whether it is still true.
• **Still to come:** *Ana dijo que la reunión es mañana.* (She said it today, and the meeting is tomorrow.)
• **A reporting verb in the present** moves nothing: *Ana dice que llega tarde*, *Ana ha dicho que llega tarde*.
• **No longer true, or never happened:** the verb must move back: *Luis dijo que se mudaría a Lima, pero no se mudó.*

items.spanish: Me dijo que vive en Lima.
items.english: He told me that he lives in Lima. (He still does.)

items.spanish: Me dijo que vivía en Lima.
items.english: He told me that he lived in Lima. (This does not say whether he still does.)

items.spanish: Ana dijo que la reunión es mañana.
items.english: Ana said that the meeting is tomorrow. (She said it today.)
Ana says that she is arriving late.

items.spanish: Luis dijo que se mudaría a Lima, pero no se mudó.
items.english: Luis said that he would move to Lima, but he did not.

sections.content: Ask one question: is it still true, or still to come, when I speak? If yes, you may keep the present. In a story, or when things have changed, move the verb back. To show that something happened earlier, use the *pluscuamperfecto*: *Dijo que había llegado el día anterior*.
